title: ProviderResponseEnvelope
description: Required response envelope for MCP tool / provider-adapter responses (architecture.md §8.2). Scope: provider/MCP tool responses only — A2A payloads carry their own separately-specified fields (§7.1–7.3), never this envelope. schema_version 1.1.0 (Checkpoint Phase 4 C.0, docs/adr/0009-phase4-checkpointc0-live-data-and-react-design.md) additively introduces optional 'capability', 'status', 'query_fingerprint', 'cache_status', and 'cache_age_seconds' -- the richer operational-status vocabulary the new live-data tools (weather, web-search evidence, flight search) need to distinguish a genuine provider failure (timeout, rate limit, provider error, cancellation) from an empty-but-successful result, which 'data_mode' alone was never designed to express. Every existing 1.0.0 instance (none of the new fields set) remains valid unchanged; this is the same additive-minor-version discipline already used by ErrorEnvelope (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0) and StayOption/FairPriceEstimate (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, docs/adr/0003-phase2-checkpoint-c0-serving-contract.md).

capability.description: 1.1.0+ only. Which capability this envelope answers (e.g. 'weather', 'web_search', 'flight_search', 'search_stays'). An open, extensible lower_snake_case vocabulary -- deliberately a pattern, not a closed enum, matching ErrorEnvelope.error_code's own open-vocabulary precedent, so a future capability never requires a schema change just to be named.

data_mode.description: 'unavailable' (1.1.0+, Checkpoint Phase 4 C.0 correction pass) means no data and no computed estimate exist at all -- distinct from 'estimated' (a genuine computed fallback exists, e.g. a Haversine distance). A timeout/rate_limited/provider_error/cancelled/unavailable status must use data_mode='unavailable' here, never 'estimated', unless an adapter actually computed a real fallback value.

status.description: 1.1.0+ only. The operational outcome of this specific call, orthogonal to data_mode (which describes the *kind* of data returned, not whether the call succeeded). Omitted on a 1.0.0 instance implies 'success' for backward compatibility with every pre-existing fixture. A provider failure must always be represented as one of the non-'success'/'partial' values here -- never as an empty 'result' object with no status signal (Checkpoint Phase 4 C.0 failure-policy requirement).

query_fingerprint.description: 1.1.0+ only. sha256 hex digest of the normalized request (see providers/fingerprint.py). Deterministic: the same logical query always produces the same fingerprint, used for cache-key construction and duplicate-call detection in a bounded ReAct loop -- never derived from wall-clock time or call order.

cache_status.description: 1.1.0+ only. Whether this result came from cache. Present only when the provider adapter has a cache layer at all.

cache_age_seconds.description: 1.1.0+ only. Age of the cached value at response time. Required whenever cache_status is 'hit' or 'stale' (dependentRequired below); meaningless for 'miss'/'bypass' and must be omitted there.
